title: Hewlett-Packard Splits in Two Today. Now What?
summary: Hewlett-Packard officially split into two separate companies. HP Inc. focuses on PCs and printing, while Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (HPE) handles servers, networking, and software, with CEO Meg Whitman leading the latter. This move aims to make both entities more agile in a changing tech market, with HPE planning potential acquisitions despite facing challenges from cloud computing rivals.

title: Amazon opens a physical bookstore, but still hopes you buy online
summary: Amazon opened its first physical bookstore, Amazon Books, in Seattle, 15 years after starting as an online bookseller. The store aims to be a physical extension of Amazon.com, allowing customers to try out Amazon devices and browse books displayed with online customer ratings. Prices in the store match online prices, and customers are encouraged to browse in-store but buy online.

title: Amazon.com is opening a real bookstore, but why?
summary: Amazon.com, after years of disrupting the traditional bookstore industry, is opening its first physical bookstore, Amazon Books, in Seattle. This move comes despite a struggling brick-and-mortar bookstore market, with declining revenues and intense competition from online retailers and independent shops. The article explores the challenges Amazon Books could face, including declining industry revenue and the continued growth of digital competition.

title: Amazon Building New Data Centers in South Korea for Cloud Unit
summary: Amazon is expanding its cloud services by building new data centers in South Korea. This new AWS region will be Amazon's 12th globally in 2016, with further expansion plans including additional data centers in China and India. The move signifies Amazon's continued growth in the cloud computing market.

title: Cord-Cutting: Hedge Funds Bet Big On Netflix; Soros, Viking Global Place New Bets
summary: Hedge funds led by George Soros’ Soros Fund Management LLC and Ole Andreas Halvorsen’s Viking Global Investors LP have made significant new investments in Netflix. Tiger Global Management LLC also substantially increased its stake in the video streaming company. These investments reflect a growing trend among investors to hedge against the traditional cable television industry, as consumers increasingly switch to streaming services, a phenomenon known as "cord cutting."

title: Hewlett Packard’s Spawn Get Off to a Slow Start
summary: Hewlett Packard's final earnings report as a combined entity revealed declining revenue, prompting its split into two companies: HP Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise. Both new companies provided financial forecasts below analyst expectations, attributing the shortfall to unfavorable exchange rates and a tough market. While HP Inc. faced challenges with printer sales to consumers affecting ink revenue, HPE showed some promise with increased server sales and a new partnership with Microsoft.

title: Amazon yank Nazi-, Imperial Japan-themed TV ads from N.Y. subway
summary: Amazon.com Inc. agreed to pull advertisements for its new television show "The Man in the High Castle" from New York City's subway system. The ads featured Nazi-inspired imagery and depicted an alternate reality where Nazi Germany and Japan control the United States after winning World War II, prompting Mayor Bill de Blasio to call for their removal.

title: Black Friday Scam: Phony Amazon App Promises Early Access to Deals
summary: A security firm discovered a phony Android app masquerading as an Amazon Black Friday deals app. This malicious app steals personal information, including text messages, call logs, and contacts, and can run up charges by auto-dialing pay-by-the-minute phone lines. Users are advised to be cautious and only download apps from official stores, as this fake app requires third-party installations and remains hidden even after the initial app is deleted.
